nodes.label: Wildlife habitat evaluation

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Wildlife habitat preservation|Wildlife habitat evaluation_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Which modeling techniques were used in the study to assess the habitat suitability of I. griffithii?
nodes.answer: The study utilized an ensemble model incorporating GLM, MARS, MaxEnt, RF, and SVM.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Wildlife habitat preservation|Wildlife habitat evaluation_qna_001
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is one drawback of relying solely on one SDM to assess habitat suitability?
nodes.answer: Relying on only one SDM can lead to substantial deviations in results by introducing biases and limiting the accuracy of predictions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Wildlife habitat preservation|Wildlife habitat evaluation_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What methodologies were used to compare morphological traits among the birds in different study areas?
nodes.answer: Morphological comparisons were made using ANOVA or the Kruskal-Wallis test.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Wildlife habitat preservation|Wildlife habitat evaluation_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What does MaxEnt do in the context of ecological niche modeling?
nodes.answer: MaxEnt compares the environmental conditions of occurrence locations of a species with those of selected background locations to assess potential areas of occurrence based on environmental similarity.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Wildlife habitat preservation|Wildlife habitat evaluation_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What method was used to calibrate and evaluate the ecological niche model?
nodes.answer: The ecological niche model was calibrated and evaluated using R with the kuenm package.
